subject: ONBOARDING: callsign modal is dismissible from console and nothing gates on having one
description: Found 2026-09-08 while triaging the P0 signup stall. CallsignModal.close() is exported publicly on window.CallsignModal (CallsignModal.js ~584) and close() is otherwise called ONLY on a successful save (~503). So during the 18-day outage a stuck user's only escape was the console, and any user can dismiss onboarding that way at will. Separately, nothing found so far GATES platform access on having a callsign - needsCallsign (FirestoreManager.js:1780) only decides whether to SHOW the modal. Measured completion collapse: Feb 93 percent of new accounts ended with a callsign, Apr 43, Jul 25, Aug 0.2, Sep 0.1. The Aug/Sep figures are confounded by bulk/class-created accounts that never see the modal, so do NOT read them as pure organic drop-off - but the Feb-to-Jul slide predates the Aug-21 bug and is its own signal worth explaining. Operator recalls an older report of users bypassing sign-in modes; the closest documented match is the still-open localStorage gate bypass in BUG_TRACKER (gate pages and the vault do not require sign-in, so a signed-out visitor keeps the bypass regardless of what the signed-in path enforces). Decide: should callsign be mandatory, and should close() stay public?
